memory_update.text: AXTI should be tracked as the clearest US-listed underfollowed InP permit-gated candidate; key survival test is whether backlog and revenue are truly constrained by export permits rather than weak end demand or execution.

UUUU is a permitted US processing-route candidate for uranium plus rare-earth/monazite supply-chain rerouting; later layers must verify commercial volumes, feedstock security, and customer qualification.
LEU maps to the uranium-fuel variant of the same pattern: the chokepoint is licensed enrichment capacity and policy rerouting away from Russian supply, not mineral reserves.
MTRN remains a speculative shadow candidate: it fits the hidden advanced-materials supplier profile, but direct controlled-mineral exposure requires primary filing verification before promotion.

For this node, the highest-value evidence is not just reserve ownership; it is proof of non-China processing, export-license dependency, customer qualification, permitted capacity, or regulatory exemptions.

node: Critical-mineral export controls, permits, and rerouted supply chains
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the idea that the chokepoint may be a permit, licensed processing route, export jurisdiction, or qualified non-China alternative supply rather than a simple mine reserve. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is AXTI because its InP exposure is explicitly tied to Chinese export permits. UUUU and LEU map to US/allied critical-material and nuclear-fuel rerouting where processing licenses, qualified facilities, and policy support matter. MTRN is included as a lower-confidence hidden-supplier hypothesis because it is classified as advanced materials rather than as a strategic critical-mineral chokepoint name.
